content.text: Sections 22.1–22.3 fully match the preferred position, and Section 23 contains only a heading with no substantive records/assurance audit path.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 meets every element of the preferred position: audits are limited to once per twelve-month period (22.1), require thirty days' prior written notice during normal business hours (22.1), are conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1), are at Vendor's cost unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent (22.2), and expressly bar Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly or unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, or other suppliers' confidential information (22.2). Section 22.3 adds Customer-favourable protections (findings are Customer Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of final report, payment resolves the issue). Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains only a heading with no substantive paragraphs, so it creates no broader audit or inspection path against Customer, and no other clause in the Agreement grants Vendor inspection, verification, or monitoring rights over Customer. No redline is required.
